title: AWS Marketplace listing copy draft (v3) — Redwood Inference
content:
Doc purpose
Draft copy blocks for AWS Marketplace listing submission for Redwood Inference. v3 incorporates PMM/Partnerships edits and tries to align to AWS Marketplace review expectations (avoid unsubstantiated performance claims, be explicit about shared responsibility, be clear on what is included in the SaaS subscription vs Dedicated/Private).

Owners / review loop
- Primary owner: Soojin (PMM)
- Partnerships review: Stephanie / Lukas
- Security wording review: Naomi / Aisha (as needed)
- Final approvers for submission: Jordan + Camila

Open questions (need answers before “final”)
1) What is the exact product name in AWS portal?
   - Options: “Redwood Inference (SaaS) – Hosted API” vs “Redwood Inference Platform”
   [Partnerships: AWS prefers the listing title to match the actual offer name in the seller portal. Keep it short.]
2) Which SKUs are exposed on AWS Marketplace at launch?
   - Hosted (metered)
   - Dedicated (contract/private offer) — may be a separate offer
   - Private (contract) — may be “Contact Us” depending on AWS constraints
   [PMM: We can mention Dedicated/Private in long description as deployment modes, but avoid implying they are purchased through the same public SaaS offer if not true.]
3) Security doc linking: which URLs are public vs “on request”?
   [Security: avoid linking internal evidence. Link to the marketplace security overview page + offer to share SOC2 report under NDA / via secure portal.]

============================================================
LISTING COPY BLOCKS (PORTAL-FRIENDLY)
============================================================

1) Listing title (working)
Redwood Inference — Production LLM inference (Hosted, Dedicated, Private)
[Partnerships: Check AWS title length limits; if too long, drop the parenthetical and keep “Production LLM inference”.]

2) Headline / short tagline (1 line)
Run and optimize large language model inference with predictable latency, cost controls, and deployment flexibility.

Alt headline options (pick 1)
A) Developer-first LLM inference for production workloads across hosted, dedicated, and private environments.
B) A unified runtime for serving LLMs with observability, rollouts, and cost/performance controls.

3) Short description (portal field)
Redwood Inference helps engineering teams serve LLMs reliably in production. Use the Redwood Hosted API for fast time-to-value, scale with Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput and isolation, or deploy Redwood Private for regulated and VPC/on-prem environments. Includes built-in observability, rollout controls, and cost/performance optimization tools.

[PMM: Avoid “best-in-class” and hard numeric claims here. Keep it procurement-friendly.]

4) Long description (portal field)
Redwood Inference is a developer-first platform for running and optimizing large language model (LLM) inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Teams choose Redwood when they need production-grade serving economics and operational control—without building and operating a custom inference stack.

What you get
- Consistent API surface across deployment modes: Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments (VPC/on-prem options)
- Production-ready inference capabilities: streaming responses, model versioning, and rollout policies (canary/A-B/fallback)
- Observability and operations: token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-model dashboards, and error analysis
- Cost/performance tooling: batching/caching guidance, model/quantization recommendations, and regression monitoring tied to eval prompt sets

Common use cases
- Customer support and agentic workflows that require predictable latency and safe rollouts
- RAG/enterprise search pipelines using embeddings and reranking
- Product experiences that need stable throughput under bursty demand (e.g., content generation, summarization, extraction)
- Regulated workloads requiring private networking, audit logging, and configurable retention

Deployment options (how customers typically buy)
- Hosted API (SaaS): Fastest onboarding. Ideal for teams getting to production quickly with usage-based consumption.
- Dedicated capacity: Reserved GPU capacity for predictable throughput and data isolation (commonly purchased via contract/private offer).
- Private deployments: VPC/on-prem options for regulated or residency-sensitive environments (commonly purchased via contract).

Getting started
1) Subscribe to the offer in AWS Marketplace.
2) Link your AWS Marketplace subscription to a Redwood organization (new org or existing).
3) Create your first API key in the Redwood Console.
4) Send a test request via SDK or REST.

Support
Support is provided by Redwood Inference. Marketplace customers receive standard support channels with options to upgrade to enterprise SLAs.

[Partnerships: Make sure “Support is provided by Redwood” matches AWS listing requirements. Also include support contact email in the dedicated portal field; below is copy-only.]

[PMM: The “Deployment options” section must not confuse a Hosted SaaS listing buyer. Consider adding a single sentence: “This AWS Marketplace offer covers the Hosted API; contact sales for Dedicated/Private.” if that’s accurate.]

5) Top customer benefits (bullets)
- Ship LLM features with predictable serving performance and clear cost controls
- Operate reliably with rollouts, fallbacks, and observability built for production
- Keep deployment flexibility: hosted for speed, dedicated for predictable capacity, private for regulated environments

6) Key features (bullets)
API + model serving
- REST/SDK interface for text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking
- Streaming responses and structured output support
- Model version pinning and controlled rollouts

Reliability + operations
- Latency and token-level cost visibility
- Per-route and per-model analytics
- Automated fallback policies to compatible model variants (where configured)

Cost/performance controls
- Workload-aware batching and caching options
- Recommendations for model/quantization profiles based on usage patterns

Security + governance (high-level)
- Encryption in transit and at rest
- Audit logging for key actions (e.g., org/user/admin events)
- Configurable retention controls for eligible data types (plan-dependent)

[Security: Replace “eligible data types” with the exact retention language we can stand behind publicly; avoid implying all request content is retained.]

============================================================
PORTAL SECTIONS / OPTIONAL BLOCKS
============================================================

7) “How it works” (compact step-by-step)
- Subscribe via AWS Marketplace.
- Complete entitlement verification and link subscription to a Redwood org.
- Create API key(s) and set usage limits/roles.
- Integrate via Redwood SDK or REST.
- Monitor usage, latency, and costs in the Redwood Console.

8) “Why Redwood” (short paragraph)
Redwood focuses on production inference economics—helping teams balance latency, reliability, and unit cost. Customers can standardize on one interface and operational toolkit while choosing the deployment model that best fits their security, procurement, and workload requirements.

9) Suggested screenshots/captions (placeholders)
- Console overview dashboard (latency + token cost breakdown)
- Model routing / rollout policy screen (canary + fallback)
- API key creation / org linking step (marketplace onboarding)
- Audit log viewer (admin events)

[PMM: Ensure we don’t show customer data in screenshots.]

============================================================
FAQ (CUSTOMER-FACING)
============================================================

Q: What does this AWS Marketplace offer include?
A: This offer provides access to Redwood’s Hosted API and Redwood Console for managing keys, usage, and observability. For Dedicated capacity and Private deployments, Redwood can provide contract options (including private offers) depending on requirements.

[Partnerships: Confirm phrasing aligns with the actual offer structure (SaaS metered vs contract).]

Q: How does billing work?
A: Charges are based on usage dimensions defined in the AWS Marketplace offer (for example, token-based or request-based dimensions depending on the SKU). Usage is metered by Redwood and reported to AWS Marketplace for billing.

[Finance/PMM note: Don’t list the exact dimensions here until final mapping is confirmed.]

Q: How do I get started after subscribing?
A: After subscribing, you’ll be guided to link your AWS Marketplace subscription to a Redwood organization in the Redwood Console. Once linked, you can create an API key and make your first request using our SDK or REST API.

Q: What happens if entitlement provisioning is delayed?
A: Entitlements can take time to propagate. If the console indicates your subscription is still processing, retry after a few minutes. If the issue persists, contact Redwood Support with your AWS subscription details so we can assist.

[Support: Add escalation guidance + expected response times in the support field, not necessarily in FAQ.]

Q: Can I link multiple AWS Marketplace subscriptions to one Redwood organization?
A: Yes—supported for customers with multiple subscriptions or accounts. Your Redwood admin can link subscriptions in the console. If you need help consolidating entitlements, contact Redwood Support.

[Eng: This must match current behavior; if not ready at launch, mark as “roadmap” or remove.]

Q: Do you store my prompts or model outputs?
A: Redwood processes request content to provide the service. Data handling and retention depend on configuration and plan. Redwood provides controls and documentation for retention and audit logging and can support additional requirements for regulated deployments.

[Security: Replace with approved “Marketplace Data Handling” language. We need a crisp statement: what we log by default, what is retained, and how customers can disable/limit.]

Q: How is data encrypted?
A: Data is encrypted in transit using TLS. Service data at rest is encrypted. For certain enterprise deployments, additional key management options may be available.

[Security: Confirm exact KMS phrasing. If we support customer-managed keys only in Private, say that explicitly.]

Q: Do you support private connectivity / VPC options?
A: Redwood supports private deployment options for customers who require VPC-based networking controls. Contact Redwood to discuss Private deployment requirements.

[Partnerships: Be careful not to imply AWS PrivateLink unless we actually offer it.]

Q: What compliance standards do you support?
A: Redwood maintains a security and compliance program aligned to industry expectations. Security documentation and evidence can be provided during procurement and security review processes.

[Security: Add: “SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA” if approved.]

Q: What models are available?
A: Redwood supports a curated catalog of popular open models and model variants suitable for production serving, with tooling to manage versions and rollouts. Model availability may vary by region and deployment mode.

[PMM: Keep this general; avoid naming specific models that might change frequently.]

Q: What regions are supported?
A: Region availability depends on deployment mode and capacity. Contact Redwood for region requirements and residency needs.

[Partnerships: If the offer is only in specific AWS regions, we may need to state that more explicitly in the listing or in a “Region support” FAQ.]

Q: How do I get support?
A: Redwood provides support directly. For standard support, contact support@redwoodinference.com. Enterprise support and SLAs are available for eligible plans.

============================================================
INTERNAL COMMENTS / WORDING TO AVOID (AWS REVIEW)
============================================================
- Avoid: “#1”, “best”, “guaranteed lowest latency”, “unlimited”, “HIPAA compliant” (unless Legal/Security approves exact wording)
- Prefer: “designed for”, “supports”, “options available”, “plan-dependent”, “contact us for requirements”

[Partnerships: AWS review flagged “guarantees” in past iterations. Keep reliability statements factual and avoid SLA claims unless the SLA is attached as an exhibit.]

============================================================
NEXT CHANGES FOR v4
============================================================
- Replace data handling FAQ with approved text from Security packet (Naomi + Alex)
- Confirm offer scope and update “What does this offer include?” (Stephanie)
- Confirm billing dimensions terminology for Hosted offer (Cole + Laura)
- Add final support language and escalation expectations (Dev Patel + Jasmine)

End.
